subject: Refrigeration and Air Conditioning
sourceFile: Technical & Trade -- REFRIGERATION AND AIR CONDITIONING.txt
examFormat: Three papers, all to be taken; Papers 1 and 2 form a composite paper taken at one sitting. Paper 1: forty compulsory multiple choice questions in 1 hour for 40 marks. Paper 2: five essay questions, any four answered in 1 hour 30 minutes for 60 marks. Paper 3: two practical questions, one answered in 2 hours for 100 marks (a list of materials is released at least two weeks earlier); if facilities are lacking, an alternative of two compulsory questions in 2 hours for 100 marks may be used, which may include free hand sketches of hand tools, circuits and wiring diagrams.
excluded: List of facilities and equipment, and suggested reading list.

topics.name: Safety and First Aid in the Workshop
objectives: State workshop rules and regulations
Identify safety devices/equipment: helmet, goggles, safety boots, hand gloves, overall, apron, sand bag, fire extinguishers
State the causes of accidents and prevention techniques
Identify first aid materials, charts, posters and first aid box
Apply first aid materials
Identify and operate various types of fire extinguishers (practical)

subtopics.name: Energy
objectives: Define energy
Describe the process of energy conversion: electrical to mechanical, gas to vapour, mechanical to heat
Explain internal energy
Explain the enthalpy of a fluid substance, its pressure, volume and temperature of internal energy
Interpret the ph diagram of a refrigerant
Demonstrate conversion of mechanical to heat energy (practical), e.g. rubbing of palms

subtopics.name: Nature of Matter
objectives: State the states of matter: solid, liquid, gas or vapour
Describe change of state of matter
Demonstrate the conversion of an ice block to water (practical)

subtopics.name: Power
objectives: Explain the meaning of power
Calculate power used by a compressor
State the units of power (watts and kilowatts) and of heat (joules and kilojoules)

subtopics.name: Temperature and its Measurement
objectives: Explain the concept of temperature
Identify different types of thermometer, e.g. gas, resistance, liquid and thermocouple
Convert temperature scales: centigrade to Fahrenheit, Celsius to Kelvin, Fahrenheit to Rankine
State the international practical temperatures: boiling point of oxygen (-182.97 degrees C), triple point of water (0.01 degrees C), boiling point of water (100 degrees C)
Plot various temperature scales

subtopics.name: Pressure and its Measurement
objectives: Explain the concept of pressure
Identify different types of pressure measuring devices, e.g. barometer, manometer, bourdon tube gauge
Measure pressure
Use suction and high pressure gauges
Demonstrate the use of a barometer and of suction and high pressure gauges to determine the performance of a refrigerant (practical)
Describe the effects of temperature, pressure and volume in refrigeration and air conditioning systems
State the gas laws: Boyle's law, Charles' law and Dalton's law
Carry out calculations involving the general gas law

subtopics.name: Introduction to Refrigeration
objectives: Describe the refrigeration cycle: evaporation, compression, condensation and expansion
Draw the layout diagram of refrigeration systems
State the types and applications of the various forms of refrigeration
Explain the principles of operation of forms of refrigeration system
State the functions of components and accessories, e.g. relay, solenoid valves, capacitors and thermostat

subtopics.name: Refrigerants
objectives: Define refrigerants and state their types
State chemical names and formulae of refrigerants
State the properties and uses of refrigerants
Identify refrigerant flow controls, e.g. TEV, AEV, capillary tube, and explain their operation
Identify refrigerants by cylinder colours (practical)

subtopics.name: Air-Conditioning Processes
objectives: State the psychometric properties of air
Describe the processes of air conditioning: heating and cooling
Explain latent and sensible heat, saturated and super-saturated vapour
Demonstrate the air conditioning principle by sling psychometer and the difference between latent and sensible heat (practical)

subtopics.name: Compressors
objectives: Identify types of compressors
Describe the construction and working principles of compressors

subtopics.name: Condensers
objectives: Describe the construction of condensers
Calculate heat load on condensers
State the types, functions and principle of operation of liquid receiver and service valves
Service a condenser (practical)

subtopics.name: Evaporators
objectives: Identify types of evaporators
Describe the construction, services and working principles of evaporators
Estimate heat load on evaporators
Service evaporators (practical)

subtopics.name: Basic Tools Used in Refrigeration and Air-conditioning Workshops
objectives: Identify basic tools: hacksaw, coil spring benders, reamers, tube cutters etc.
State the tools and procedures for servicing a window unit air-conditioner
Service a window air-conditioner (practical)

subtopics.name: Fault Diagnosis and Trouble Shooting
objectives: Describe different methods of diagnosing faults: systematic and observation
Identify common faults in refrigeration systems and their symptoms: leakage, faulty units, faulty compressor, poor cooling and current leakage

subtopics.name: Maintenance and Testing
objectives: Describe techniques of effective repairs and trouble shooting in refrigeration and air-conditioning systems
Test for leakages, polarity, insulation continuity, pressure and efficiency (practical)
Maintain compressors, evaporators, motors, condensers, valves, accumulators and contactors
Repair faults in compressors, evaporators, motors and condensers (practical)

subtopics.name: Piping, Ducting and Trunking
objectives: Explain the concept of piping, ducting and trunking
Pipe a condenser and an evaporator
Describe ducting, trunking and installation of air-conditioners
Identify piping, ducting and trunking tools: mallet hammer, flaring tools, silver tape, dot-punch, bending spring, amaflex, hacksaw, PVC pipes
Install a split air-conditioner (practical)

subtopics.name: Motors and Generators
objectives: State the types, functions, operations and application of motors and generators
Describe installation procedures for motors and generators
Maintain motors and generators in a refrigeration system
Service motors and generators (practical)

subtopics.name: Cold Room
objectives: Explain the working principles of a cold room
Describe cold room installation procedures
Identify factors affecting cold room operations

topics.name: Insulation Processes
objectives: State the importance of insulation of refrigeration and air-conditioning systems
Identify types of insulating materials: glasswool, fibre glass, polystyrene foam, wood, bitumen, ceramic etc.
State the functions and properties of insulation materials
Describe the procedure for insulating refrigeration and air-conditioning systems

subtopics.name: Business Concept
objectives: Explain the concept of business enterprise and types of businesses: sole proprietorship, partnership, limited liability etc.
Identify sources of finance: loan, mortgage, shares, overdrafts, savings etc.

subtopics.name: Marketing
objectives: State the types and functions of marketing styles
Describe meaningful marketing at the least cost
Explain marketing protocol and cost
Carry out a commercial marketing survey to set up a refrigeration and air-conditioning business (practical)

subtopics.name: Accounting
objectives: State the principles of accounting
Explain the concept of business as a separate entity
Prepare a ledger, trial balance and balance sheet
